topics.title: The poet, his purpose and the call to keep still

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Pablo Neruda and the purpose of the poem: quiet introspection and mutual understanding.
Explain why the poet asks everyone to count to twelve, keep still and not speak in any language.
Interpret the 'exotic moment' of togetherness without rush or engines.

topics.title: Harm to nature and to oneself

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the image of fishermen and whales shows man's exploitation of nature.
Interpret how the salt gatherer looking at his hurt hands shows neglected self-awareness.
Interpret the poet's images of green wars, wars with gas and fire, and 'victory with no survivors'.
Explain how the moment of quiet could turn war-makers towards peace and brotherhood.

topics.title: Stillness is not inactivity: the sadness of not understanding

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the poet wants introspection, not total inactivity or death.
Identify the 'sadness' of never understanding ourselves and threatening ourselves with death.

topics.title: The Earth as teacher and the form of the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the symbol of the Earth that seems dead and later proves to be alive.
Recognise the poem's free verse, varying line lengths and its framing by the count to twelve.
